utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. It's unusual that the Chamber is announced twice by knocking on the door three times, but, Mr. Dutertre, the Chamber received after the first three knocks the following information that a new request for subpoena has been filed, two subpoenas. That upon further inquiry by the Chamber, the Chamber thought at the time might be too short for a subpoena to be executed. The Chamber was informed that the OTP was informed by those responsible for issuing such subpoena that the time was too short to have it executed, so therefore the Chamber is surprised that it receives a request for subpoenas of which the OTP is informed that it could not be executed been the time-limits set by the Chamber, that's one. The second is that it would certainly damage the reputation of this Chamber if it would happen again as happened with the early subpoenas that the parties, in this case the OTP, provides the Chamber with wrong addresses so that we issue subpoenas where addresses are mixed up, and I take it that the OTP would not expect the Chamber before issuing a subpoena to verify the correctness of the addresses to see whether they're mixed up. And if it was not one incident in a long list of incidents where lack of precision has struck the Chamber several times, I would not have used these rather strong words in court today. Then I'd like to deliver a decision. There's no problem if the witness is present, it's about the five out of the six exhibits. Mr. Emmerson, unless there was something else, I thought you were rising -- no. But then have the booths -- yes, of the oral decision. The Chamber will now give its decision on the admission of Exhibits P1205 through to P1209. The parties will recall that yesterday on the 31st of October, 2007 -- yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I just wanted to extend my apologies. I think that there was a mix-up in the addresses indeed between the two applications, but as for the remainder I shall refer this to Mr. Re for further instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You interrupted me when I was delivering a decision, but since it was to apologise, I do not mind that much. So therefore the Chamber will now give its decision on the admission of the exhibits P1205 through to P1209 and the parties will, as I just said, will recall that on the 31st of October, 2007, yesterday, at the start of the current witness's testimony, the Chamber announced that the Prosecution had shown goods cause for adding these six, six documents longer to its 65 ter exhibit list. You'll find that at transcript page 10056. The Prosecution then tendered five out of these six documents which were subsequently marked for identification as Exhibits P1205 through to P1209. The Chamber informed the parties that it would decide on the admission of these documents once it had had a time to review their content. The Chamber has now thoroughly reviewed the contents of these documents. In doing so, the Chamber has been mindful that the translation of these documents were only disclosed to the Defence on the evening of the 29th of October, less than 48 hours before they were tendered by the Prosecution. The Chamber, however, stresses that late disclosure is not a bar to admission. However, the Defence should be allowed sufficient time to investigate and properly prepare to cross-examine on the materials. With regard to the documents in question, the Chamber finds that the content for which they are being introduced is not pivotal to the case and adds little to the evidence already before the Chamber. Therefore, rather than recalling the witness once the Defence has had time to properly prepare to cross-examine on these documents, the Chamber in this case denies the admission of documents P1205 through to P1209. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, then I'd like to remind you, as I always do if a witness returns the next day, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, can I ask you, please, to turn to paragraph 14 in your witness statement, and just so that we're sure that there's no translation difficulty, could you read out for us, please, in B/C/S the last sentence in paragraph 14 so that the interpreters can give us a live translation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, exceptionally I'll allow you to do it, but it's -- if there's any doubt as far as translation is concerned, then it's usually not the interpreters who are supposed either to correct or to verify the -- that's a kind of a standard rule. Nevertheless, I will allow you to ask the witness to read this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's simply foundation to make sure that I don't put a question on a false premise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's the purpose, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just read that last sentence out for us, Mr. Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The police did not dare go into parts of the Dukadjini area, such as Pec, Kapesnica, Drenica, Jablanica, Djakovica, and other villages." As I said yesterday, some of the formulations may have been unfortunate perhaps in this translation. It should have read: In other parts, such as Pec, Kapesnica, Drenica, Jablanica, Djakovica, and other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now do understand that the translation is correct but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The witness now says that his formulation of -- in the 92 ter statement was not perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You weren't intending to say that the police had any difficulties entering Pec and Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police had problems. It reads here that they did not dare go there because of such problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Even in Pec?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Particularly in the settlement of Kapesnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Djakovica as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We know that there was a military and police presence based in Pec, Mr. Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a police station in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which remained open throughout 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did remain open; however, it had to work with a number of dangers that were present there on a daily basis, fire-arms were being discharged regularly, ambushes organized, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Let me see if I've understood. Are you intending to suggest that the police did not enter the municipality of Pec outside the town and the municipality of Djakovica, or are you intending to convey here that the police didn't dare to enter the towns themselves? It's a little difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and clarify. The settlement or neighbourhood of Kapesnica is a part of Pec, just above Pecka Bistrica. Exclusively or perhaps 99,9 per cent inhabited by Albanians. There may have been a few Serbian houses. The same goes for Drenica and Jablanica. In Djakovica there were less than 1 per cent of Serbs, Montenegrins, and other nationalities. There were also neighbourhoods and settlements exclusively populated by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to move on unless the Trial Chamber wants the matter pursued any further. Can we look briefly at paragraph 38 of your witness statement, Mr. Gojkovic, where you refer to having been present during the recovery of human remains and items of clothing in a place called Bandera in Dasinovac. Now, we have seen a videotape of a number of men including, so we have been told, yourself in the area of Bandera during the course of the recovery of these items. And also on the video we're able to see -- I'm not going to play it because we've all watched it before - a man who is apparently in handcuffs and under detention who has been identified by other witnesses as a man called Zenelj Alija. Do you remember there being a person who was in detention, police detention, present at the time you were there in Bandera?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim it for certain that once I was at the location during the on-site investigation, I saw no detained persons whatsoever -- at least I did not notice anyone. I think I also owe you an explanation, and by your leave I'd like to read out something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you're reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An excerpt from the Law on Criminal Procedure, authorising various bodies of the Ministry of the Interior to collect information even from people who are currently detained. Whether the procedure and treatment of that person was respected if such a person indeed existed there can be seen from the contents of the documents that had to do with those activities, with the people who participated. Perhaps I can read out the part of the law that refers to that if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether the legal issue is something that bothers Mr. Emmerson at this moment, so thank you for your offer but Mr. Emmerson will put, I take it, some precise questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you can just focus, Mr. Gojkovic, not on the law that you're looking at but on the question that I'm asking you. And your evidence as I understand it is whilst you were there at Bandera there was to your knowledge no person who was arrested or detained present there at the same time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. When I was there on the first day, the 9th of September, 1998, there was nobody. Whether anyone was detained before that, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't want you to get confused, Mr. Gojkovic. Did you not say in your 92 ter statement that it was the 10th of September - have I misunderstood? - the 10th of September when you went to Dashinoc, Bandera?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 10th of September; however, the on-site investigation concerning the entire incident, including Lake Radonjic, Dasinovac, and the farm was initiated on the 9th of September and concluded on the 19th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, just --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a number of documents testifying to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Don't worry about the documents for the moment, Mr. Gojkovic, and don't worry about the 9th of September or anywhere else. I was asking you about the 10th of September when you say you were present at Dashinoc, Bandera, and for the absolute clarity of the record, to your recollection no detained person was there at the same time you were, is that right, in Bandera?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said already - and I can only repeat - I do not remember seeing such a person --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when we were carrying out the on-site investigation at Bandera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And could you turn to paragraph 90, please, in your statement. Do you have paragraph 90 there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 90 you refer to annex 10, and I'll just read it for the record so that we're clear. You say: "Documents relating to two people who pointed out the Lake Radonjic scene to the police are at annex 10." Now, pause for a moment. Annex 10 to your witness statement contains a number of documents including a power of attorney for the representation of two men called Zenelj Alija and Naser Kalamashi. My question is: How did you know that these were the two people who had pointed out the Lake Radonjic scene to the police?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try and answer this question. As I stated yesterday, as of November 1998, I was elected president of the district court in Pec. As of the moment when the procedure was initiated in this case, all documentation that was requested by the district court in Pec went through my hands, since I headed that institution. Therefore, I forwarded the Kalamashi case and others. There are names there of judges and everyone else involved. It went through the Ministry of Justice or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through the office in Belgrade, to the people responsible at this Tribunal. As for any other activities, who did what, what judge was involved, when those persons were first detained, whether by the SUP or the court, there must be written evidence on all that. There should be a decision on detention, on the extension of detention, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gojkovic, again, if I can just focus the question and your answer down a little bit, please. My question was specifically how did you personally come to know that these two men were said to have pointed out the Lake Radoniq canal to the police? Simply how did you come to know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to know that at the point when they asked for the case file and when they told me why they were asking for it. Besides that, during the hearing before me there was a discussion about adducing evidence to the effect that there was some persons who pointed to where the crime site was. It was when I was assigned that case that this discussion was carried out. I had no way of coming to know this through any other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause, please. Thank you. So it was during the hearing for the detention of these men that you found out that they had allegedly pointed the canal out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to explain this. First I was asked about how the organs of the interior came to arrive at the crime scene. I was asked whether I asked the members of the Ministry of the Interior about this, and I will answer this question. I had never learnt this from them nor did I have the authority to ask any such information from them. The appropriate legislation prescribes what the Ministry of the Interior does, what the judiciary does, and what ultimately an investigating judge does.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, could I just ask you to stop for a moment, please. On the transcript, page 10, line 5, your answer is recorded as follows: "Besides that, during the hearing before me there was a discussion about adducing evidence to the effect that there was some persons who pointed to where the crime site was." What is the hearing that you are there referring to, please? Just answer that question for me. What hearing were you there referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you put the question once more to me. Is that my statement, my testimony, page 10, line 5, or are you referring to some written document? So is that my statement, is that my testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's your testimony today, Mr. Gojkovic. Mr. Emmerson read from the transcript that is made immediately once you've spoken words. Perhaps I -- perhaps you read it again so that it's in the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said: "Besides that" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said in the context --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Perhaps you repeat the previous line as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question I asked you was how did you come to know about these men having been said to have pointed out the canal to the police. You replied: "I came to know that at the point when they asked for the case file, and when they told me they were asking for it. Besides that, during the hearing before me there was a discussion about adducing evidence to the effect that there was some persons who pointed to where the crime site was. It was when I was assigned that case that this discussion was carried out. I had no way of coming to know this through any other sources." My questions, Mr. Gojkovic, are, first of all: What was the hearing; and secondly: When were you assigned the case?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows from what I just heard that there must have been a misunderstanding. I was referring to the case -- this particular case where I'm appearing right now, Ramush Haradinaj et al. It was in relation to this particular case that I was called by the prosecutors from their office in Belgrade. Among other matters, there was a discussion there about the fact that there was some evidence about persons who indicated where the crime scene was. In response to that I said that I didn't know anything about that. Later on a case file was asked for and it was delivered. I don't know anything more about it. The file contains information about when these persons were placed into custody, for how long, when they appeared before a court of law, and how the proceedings went on from there. That's all I know. If you want me to repeat about that particular case involving the individuals, who pointed to where the crime scene was, I have no knowledge. So I have no knowledge about that. I allow for the possibility that if their detention was extended after the 18th of November, 1998, at the point in time when I was elected president of the court, I know that I was one of the judges on the bench. I was in fact the presiding judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So are we to understand the position to be this, Mr. Gojkovic, that before being asked to look at papers to assist the Office of the Prosecutor, you had no idea who had pointed the canal out to the police; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm categorically stating again that I neither know who reported this to the police nor did I ask them about it. Pursuant to the criminal procedure law, the police have their authorities and their method of proceeding, and I know that pursuant to that legislation they are allowed to keep a person in custody for three days. Upon the expiry of the three days, they can either release that individual or file a criminal report against that person, from which point this matter lies within the hands of the prosecutor's office, or rather, the court. Should the prosecutor ask for an investigation to be carried out, the court would act within the legislation, collect evidence, hear witnesses. And at the end of that, or rather, the police force would be doing the investigation, interviewing suspects, gathering evidence, at the end of which process they would refer the matter to the relevant prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, if you carefully listen to the questions of Mr. Emmerson, you'll find that he's more interested in hearing more about factual situation at the time rather than what was within whose competence at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So would you please very much focus your answers, answers on what Mr. Emmerson ask you. And Mr. Emmerson is invited if he quotes literally from the record, especially if it's the testimony of the witness, that he should do it precisely. The word "why" disappeared when you read. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that must have been my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You remember, Mr. Gojkovic, making a statement to the Prosecution in this matter in May of 2006?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it was a statement taken in English but translated to you into B/C/S; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Without bringing it up on the screen, because it's a relatively short passage from paragraph 34 of the statement that I want to ask you about, you say in your witness statement this, you say: "I don't know who informed the SUP that the bodies were at Lake Radonjic. It is not the responsibility of the investigative judge to ask the police how they discovered the bodies." And then a little later on you say this: "I never heard later, either directly or indirectly, if the scene had been pointed out by someone to the police." Now, does that accurately record the position in fact, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely what I'm confirming to you today. As I attended the scene and in the period after that I had never asked the police force who had given them the indication as to where the crime scene was. I had never asked them that and I don't know this today. I didn't ask them that because I did not have the authority to do so. It is up to others to assess whether they in performing their duties have been adhering to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we understand, you say that despite being appointed as the investigative judge for this crime scene, it was not part of your function to discover how it had been found by the police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer that question. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection because the question was put to the question [as interpreted] on several occasions in various forms, indeed, but it boils down to the same thing. And the witness has already answered and has repeated that he had already provided an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the last answer -- the witness several times has expressed that it was not within his authority to question anyone about how they went there. I think he spontaneously included this in his answer. Mr. Emmerson is entitled to further explore the basis for that part of the answer. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply want you to clarify for me, Mr. Gojkovic, yes or no, whether I have correctly understood your evidence, that despite being appointed as the investigative judge for this crime scene, you say it was not part of your function to make inquiries about how the police had discovered it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my answer: I was not appointed an investigating judge. An investigating judge is designated for every calendar year. This is the way we proceed. That's number one. Number two, I don't know because I never asked, and I never endeavoured to learn who told the police where that site was, where a very, very tragic event happened. If you'll allow me to, I will read out provision of the law regulating the authorities of an organ of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, I think what Mr. Emmerson would like to know is that whether in your capacity if you would have wished to do so, perhaps you may have had no reasons to do it, but if you had wished to ask the police officers how -- how they learned that there would have been a crime scene at the Lake Radonjic canal, whether you had the competence to ask that to the police officers. That's I think the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my categorical statement. I did not have the authority under the law to put such a question. Let me explain. The SUP organs have their methods of discovering and detecting and uncovering the perpetrators of criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if I may follow that up then, leaving aside your legal authority, in all the time that you were down there no one mentioned it to you either by chance in conversation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Nobody mentioned that, including me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If a man in detention had been present with you at Bandera, would you expect to have been told that this was a person in custody being brought to the scene to point out a crime scene?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, can you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If the position is, Mr. Gojkovic - and obviously we have other evidence in this case - if the position is that there was, in fact, a person in custody present at the same time as you were at Bandera on the 10th near Dasinovac, a person who was in custody having allegedly pointed out the crime scene to the police and if he was there at the same time as you were, would you expect to be informed about who he was?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the assumption that that individual was present at the time when we were conducting an on-site investigation at Dasinovac, I categorically state that I would not be told that that individual was present. This again for the reasons I stated before. That's why I believe it would be a good thing to read out the relevant provision from the Law on Criminal Procedure regulating the way in which the organs of the interior proceed in relation to persons in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, don't worry about the procedure. If you would like at the end of your testimony to give us a list of legislative provisions for us to consult, then please do so. The questions I'm asking you essentially are questions of fact and practice. Again let me put one further question to you in this regard. If you had seen a man there in handcuffs or under detention, would you not have asked what he was doing there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Because that individual would not yet be within our jurisdiction. He was still within the jurisdiction -- he would still be within the jurisdiction of the MUP organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at annex 9, please, to your witness statement which has been provisionally marked for identification as P1200.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've had some discussions with the registry about practicalities. May I indicate to the Trial Chamber that this document or this annex consists of two documents, an indictment against Bekim Kalamashi, Zenelj Alija, and others, and then a court judgement in respect of the same group of individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn in your file, Mr. Gojkovic, to annex 9, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we could start by pulling up page 1 just to identify the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see -- I think perhaps you can just help us with this. This is an indictment dated the 5th of March, 1999, against a number of named individuals, the first of whom is Zenelj Alija and the second of whom is Bekim Kalamashi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And of course by this time you had been president of the district court in Pec for something like about five months, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could turn briefly to the next page in each, so it's page 2 of the B/C/S, page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do we see after the list of names a short description of the reasons for the indictment under the heading: "Because," correct? A short summary of what they're accused of.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The -- just bear with me a moment. Wait for the question, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The English, I'm afraid, spreads over two pages at this stage. The B/C/S section that appears in the right-hand section of the screen is partial -- partially translated on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've read these documents, Mr. Gojkovic, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to take it shortly without going through the detail. This was a group of men who had been arrested in the village of Kodralija at the beginning of September; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly where they were detained. It's in the file, and the criminal offence was committed in the village of Kodralija during the month of May 1998, in the manner as described therein. This is a description of the criminal offence under Article 136, and that's conspiring for enemy activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll come to that in a moment. If I can just summarize the allegation. Essentially they're charged under Article 136(2), which I think is the offence that you refer to in paragraph 11 of your 92 ter statement in which you describe it as a charge of persons coming together to take part in hostile activities for terrorist crimes, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not describing it, it's the prosecutor describing the offence because the prosecutor issues the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there seems to be a misunderstanding. Mr. Emmerson takes you back to your own statement where you summarize or describe what these people were charged with, of course charged with by the prosecution at that time, but you describe it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I just correct that to this extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The passage at paragraph 11 describes the nature of that offence as a common charge, but it's the 136(2) criminal offence. So it's an offence of associating to take part in hostile activities. And we can see, I think, from the indictment that the allegation is that, in short, these men joined the KLA, brought fire-arms in from Albania, and stood guard in the village of Kodralija. Would you agree that that's a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could just turn, please, to the statement of reasons which is on the following page of the English text, so the next page of the English text, and appears on the following page also of the B/C/S text. Now, under the heading "statement of reasons," we can see a paragraph that reads: "The investigation, conducted by the investigating judge of the district court in Pec for criminal case number Kio No. 182/98, has established the facts from which it follows that the accused Zenelj Alija and the others have committed the criminal offences they were charged with as per the disposition of this indictment." My first question, Mr. Gojkovic, is where it refers to the investigating judge, can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating judge who conducted the investigation?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's stated in the case file. I can't really remember. There were many cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Was it you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that either. If there exist minutes or records of this particular case, then I would have had to be the one signing them if that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You have no recollection of whether it was you or not; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't remember. The case file tells you exactly who the investigating judge was because you can -- there you have the investigation-related documents, trial documents, and of course the file of the appeals proceedings. There you have the name of the investigating judge and of course also the judges on the bench, including the presiding bench -- the presiding judge of the bench. And the case file exists and it can be obtained at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We'll come to the judgement in a moment or two. Do you now, Mr. Gojkovic, have any recollection of a group of men being arrested in Kodralija and charged in respect of this indictment? Is that anything you've got any independent recollection of at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember what I said before, and I'll repeat it again. I remember having -- having been dealing with a great deal of reports to this Tribunal, to the Belgrade office, to the Ministry of Justice in Serbia, because I recall that we had to submit monthly, bimonthly, sixth-monthly reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, we are limited in our time. There's a clear question whether apart from what we find in documents which would allow us to reconstruct the positions at the time, whether you have any memory at this moment on this specific case, including a group of youngsters, I think they were relatively young men, involved in crimes committed in Kodralija. Do you have any recollection apart from the paperwork?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. If we could just drop down to the next paragraph briefly, we can see "the accused Zenelj Alija," it says, "when questioned in the course of the investigation," and then it sets out what he's recorded as having said. When those words appear in an indictment "when questioned in the course of the investigation," does that mean questioned by the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would they have come to the investigating judge from police custody?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've explained this already, but let me tell you again. It's the MUP bodies that take the statement, and they submit the criminal report to the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as there is a request for investigation the investigating judge --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it might be very helpful for the purposes of time if you would be kind enough just to watch me, and if you're not answering the question I'm asking you I'll let you know with a wave of the hand. The question I'm asking you is a simple one. When somebody -- and I think you've looked at this indictment and already expressed an opinion to Mr. Dutertre yesterday about this in relation to these individuals. When these individuals were brought before the investigating judge for questioning, would they have been in custody?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were in custody, they had to, or rather, if they had been in custody, they would have had to be -- to have been brought over from custody, how else?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And after the questioning, they would be returned to the custody of the MUP, would they?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very simple --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the MUP, they would be held at the investigative prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very simple, exactly. If we can just look at the following paragraph, for which we need to look at the next page of the B/C/S, but it remains on the same page of the English translation. We can see -- and if I can just note it for the record that the accused Bekim Kalamashi when questioned during the investigation has completely denied having been a member of the KLA, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the indictment, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now if we can move, please, to the judgement which in the annex I think begins in the B/C/S on page 6, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I can take this very briefly. You read this document as well presumably, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. In short, this group of men were each convicted of the charge against them of membership and association with the KLA, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we can just move to the statement of reasons in respect of that which appears - just bear with me just a moment - I'm sure you can find it a few pages further on in the B/C/S version. Do you have it there? I think it should be page 11 for the e-court and the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And page 12 of the English translation, that's at page 15.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Try to keep it side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could look, please, go over the page in the English but remain where we are in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see in the second paragraph of the statement of reasons that the defence advanced by Bekim Kalamashi was a denial of membership of the KLA, correct? It's the second paragraph under the statement of reasons. You can see it on the screen in front of you, Mr. Gojkovic, if it's easier, second paragraph there. Sorry. Can I stop you for a moment because it's not a very complicated question. If you look at the second paragraph, Mr. Gojkovic, does it record on the statement of reasons that the accused Bekim Kalamashi in his defence has explained that he has never been a member of the KLA of the village of Kodralija? Is that what it says? Mr. Gojkovic, can I suggest that you look on the screen in front of you. Look at the second paragraph on the right-hand side of the screen. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally in relation to this judgement, if we could look, please, and I'm just going to take it on the English, we need to move to the following page. And in the B/C/S - bear with me one moment - yes, if we can just look to the bottom of the English side of the screen for the moment. And in the B/C/S, I'll just have to give you a page number in just one moment. Yes, it's the bottom of the following page in B/C/S. We can see that there is there recorded the alleged partial confession given by Zenelj Alija in the pre-trial proceedings, correct? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just look, please, to the bottom of that paragraph, so in both documents we need to move over one page to the last sentence of the paragraph dealing with Zenelj Alija.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see that, just if you look at the very last sentence of that first paragraph on page 8 -- again, Mr. Gojkovic, it might be easier for you to look at the screen, it's the right-hand side of the screen, the last four lines of the B/C/S of the paragraph that appears there, we can see that at his trial Mr. Alija maintained that what had been said -- I'll read the English translation as it appears: "At the trial the accused has explained, apart from his previous statement, that he said all that in fear of police and that on the critical occasion he has not joined the 'KLA.'" . Now, that formulation, and I won't go through each example, appears in the judgement in respect of a number of the individuals there that statements had been made on the grounds of fear of the police. But there appears to be no record in the judgement of what the basis for that was or what it was that the accused was saying had been done to them to cause them to be in fear of the police. My question is: Would you normally expect there to be a record of the grounds for such a fear being expressed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the judgement what is stated there is the position of his defence according to the Law on Criminal Procedure in our country, an accused can remain silent, in which case the court is duty-bound to warn him that that may worsen his position. He can lie or tell the truth. In all three cases the court is duty-bound to check all defence allegations and compare that to appropriate evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. For example, we heard evidence from one of the police officers who handled these men that Bekim Kalamashi and certainly some of this group were brought into the police station in their underwear. Is that the sort of thing you would expect a court to inquire into when allegations of this kind are raised in someone's defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is stated, such allegations had to be checked and verified. If somebody resorted to such activities, they had to be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, the witness has started already answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sorry could you tell us which line you were talking about to facilitate everyone's work. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: 6626, lines 11 to 13, the testimony of Mr. Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if that were the position you would expect that to be recorded in the judgement, Mr. Gojkovic, would you not?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When an accused changes his statement, the court needs to ask the accused why that has happened and it has to be supported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, I think Mr. Emmerson would like to know where the judgement says that at trial the accused have -- the accused in this case has explained that in fear of the police he admitted certain matters which he doesn't admit anymore in court, whether the court would have further inquired into what made him to fear the police, what had happened that he was fearful, whether it was -- could you tell us whether that was usually and perhaps specifically in this case explored.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To repeat, a confession or denial of guilt when interrogated by the police has no effect on the proceedings itself. During the proceedings, starting with the investigating judge and ending with the main hearing, the accused can state freely what his position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not my question, Mr. Gojkovic. What I asked you is that if someone comes in court and says: I gave a false statement to the police because I was afraid, would you then further inquire why that person was afraid or said that he was afraid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, an accused can confess anything to the police, for example, out of fear or pressure, but once before an investigating judge he can deny all that. He can say: All that I had said is not true, and then he can say what he believes to be true. After that, the court needs to compare that with existing evidence and to conduct a hearing or inquire into the treatment of the accused and in order to arrive at the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was there any inquiry into the treatment of the police here where this accused says that he gave his statement out of fear and not in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you anything about that. Such data should be contained in the case file. The judge in charge of the case was duty-bound by the law to ask the accused on these circumstances, to pose questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, whether we could find it in the file is another matter, but we would like to know whether you have any memory specific on this. And it turns out that you could not answer that question would consulting the documents. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you one question on that subject, Mr. Gojkovic. Did you ever come across in all your time as an investigating judge in Kosovo, did you ever come across allegations that people were beaten in police custody, then brought before the investigating judge under threat by the police that unless they repeated what they said in the police station they would be beaten again when they got back there? Did you ever come across such cases where that was alleged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think this is a difficult question because you would presuppose that the person would go back after --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- Being interrogated. And this is what the witness denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No I think we may be at cross-purposes. I think the evidence of the witness is that he would go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think he --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well then we should clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My understanding of the witness's testimony, without having a transcript in front of me, because I sought to clarify that very question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It was a little quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll find a line and a page for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I wanted to draw your attention to that last piece of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that the answer wasn't as clear as I had recalled it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The answer was clearly the opposite. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, can I just put the question to you again because there seems to be potential confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's a compound question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When somebody was arrested on a charge under Article 136 of terrorism and brought before the investigating judge, after the questioning was finished, assuming there was thought to be a case against them, what would happen to them? Where would they go?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the hearing, the investigating judge decides whether there is any legal foundation to conduct further investigation into prolonged detention. If there is a request in place by the prosecutor to keep the person in detention, a decision is made on detention of up to one month, and that person is then returned to the investigating prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I just wanted to noted that the question that was asked by Mr. Emmerson at page 23, line 4, and the answers follow from there up until line 11 in accordance precisely with Mr. Emmerson's recollection just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the -- what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Line 11 was expressly that the witness then said not the MUP, they would be held at the investigative prison, and this is said now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who would be responsible for holding them at the investigative prison, Mr. Gojkovic? Who would take them there and who would hold them there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who work at the pre-trial detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who were they, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Employees of the district court of Pec, its pre-trial detention department.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. They're not MUP officers? They're not employed by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next question perhaps relevant, Mr. Emmerson, would be: Once they were then taken to -- to the investigative prison, would the MUP have access to that prison to further interview those accused or would they be excluded from further approaching the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The law strictly prescribes that without an approval of the investigating judge in charge, not a single employee of the SUP, be it an inspector or another official, cannot or is not to have any access to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was such permission often given? Was that routine or was that exceptional?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, there was some instances, but the procedure was followed in general. If someone was in breach of the procedure, they should be held accountable; however, the law is clear on that. Throughout my career, I never allowed for such behaviour and no one asked me to do anything regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, the law says, as far as I understand you, that you need permission. Now, my question was whether such permission for SUP officers to further interview an accused when he was in an investigative prison, whether that was frequently granted or whether that was exceptional. I'm talking about frequency rather than about violating rules.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, it only happened in exceptional circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally on this topic, can I ask you this: Did you ever come across cases where it was alleged that people had been threatened by the officers who beat them to repeat what they had said to the police when they appeared before the investigating judge? Is that something that you became aware of as an allegation that was made at any time in general?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to object to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has stated that as far as the relevant case is concerned, that he remembered this agreement was not given, but he cannot answer in general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the interests of time I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because I have one or two other topics to cover. I'm conscious of the time I've been given.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One or two questions about the canal itself, please, if I may; and then I'll just come back to one other issue of procedure. Paragraph 30 in your witness statement, could you turn to that, please, and help us with that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we've changed topic, but sorry. I was not quite exactly translated. Lines 23 to 25 on page 32 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Mr. Dutertre just repeated what he had said, the problem was that the interpreter was lagging behind when he started taking the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Dutertre, you objected against the question. Mr. Emmerson, hearing your objection, announced that he would move on. Is there any specific reason why we -- where there's no contested issue here, whether we would need to know or repeat what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not going to repeat. I just wanted to say that I was not accurately reflected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to take these questions as quickly as I can for the next section, please, Mr. Gojkovic. Paragraph 30, your statement reads, and this describes your arrival on the 9th of September: "I observed bodies covered with soil by the wall of the canal, and I could see flies around the bodies. A bad smell was in the air. I crossed the canal and saw more bodies and body parts." When you say the -- you crossed the canal, can you just explain to us from which side of the canal you began to cross and from which side -- to which side of the canal you made your crossing; in other words, which direction you were going.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the west to the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say "I crossed the canal and saw more bodies and body parts," where did you see the additional bodies and body parts after you'd crossed the canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the canal itself just -- just at the point where the concrete part of the canal ends and there is a small waterfall there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So having crossed the canal, you didn't see any bodies on the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no bodies outside the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's a slightly ambiguous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you mean there were no bodies on the opposite side of the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came to the plateau of the canal. There is a concrete part of it. After that there is the waterfall. Further up from the plateau where we had come from there is a pedestrian crossing, a sort of a bridge made of planks. We crossed that bridge and went along one edge of the canal on our left-hand side looking towards Lake Radonjic. Just blow or at the foot of the waterfall there was an Opel passenger vehicle that was on its roof and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer's clear enough. Thank you very much. We've understood your answer. Paragraph 36, you're dealing there with the 10th of September, and in the second sentence you say: "We found bodies in the concrete canal, in the canyon in front of and behind the Opel car and we walked right to the mouth of Lake Radonjic." Now, you describe bodies in the concrete canal and in the canyon. Can you help us with this, please, does it follow from that that on the 10th when you were there you remember seeing bodies in the concrete section of the canal itself?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the very fact I mentioned yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that some of the formulations are wrong. In the concrete part of the canal there were no bodies. Where were they found exactly? Well, that is all reflected in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can corroborate that by pointing out another technical error --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, can I interrupt you a second. Do we then take it that whenever you say in this statement I saw concrete bodies in the canal, that is wrong --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Concrete bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I saw bodies in the concrete canal, Mr. Gojkovic, you say that I think --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "concrete" is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've got another topic to deal with. I wonder if I could very briefly before asking for a break ask Judge Gojkovic to look at a short passage of videotape, Mr. Gojkovic to look at a short passage of videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that. Yesterday I gave some instructions on how to address him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that was an error, a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's you, Mr. Gojkovic, at the Bandera site, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is fully correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just wondering whether seeing the gentleman in the passage of video that immediately preceded that with the beard prompted your recollection at all about a gentleman being in custody?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just wind back a little bit so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please rewind back.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see that gentleman there? Pausing there. Do you see that gentleman there? Is he somebody you saw at the time at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it is very likely that the man was there. There were many people there. I cannot remember who, in what capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of clarity, Your Honour, could we have the reference of this video and the exact length when it starts and when it finishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The passage playing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Clearly state --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The passage played I'm told is Exhibit P72, and it begins at 45.07 on the counter and continues to 45.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the time, whether correct or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the last portion played, rewound is 3.08 a.m., 11 of September, 1998, whether true or not is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's what appears on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you give us an indication?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I inquire with other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My examination will be shorter than I expected it to be. Obviously some of the questions propounded. We are organizing some things. It should be no longer than half an hour and it could be shorter than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I will have little if anything to ask after Mr. Guy-Smith is finished, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break and we'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to turn into private session. [Private session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber would like to announce two decisions. The first decision is related to the recalling of Witness 55. The Chamber has decided not to recall this witness. Written reasons for our decision will be given in due course. The parties are hereby asked to make submissions on the status of the evidence already given by this witness in court by next Thursday, the 8th of November. The Defence of all three accused is informed that the Chamber received information in relation to this matter from VWS which was addressed to the Chamber and also to the Prosecution. Since there's no specific reason for just addressing the Prosecution, the Chamber will send this after having consulted with VWS, a copy of this e-mail to the Defence. The second decision concerns Witness 15. The Chamber has decided to deny the subpoena for this witness. Written reasons for this decision will also be given in due course, and this includes the Chamber's rulings on these matters. Now I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then finally I will deliver a decision on the Prosecution's application for videolink testimony for Shefqet Kabashi. On the 25th of October, 2007, the Prosecution asked the Chamber to consider four options to secure Mr. Kabashi's evidence. The four options included an application for compelled videolink testimony from Mr. Kabashi's country of residence. On the 29th of October of this year, the Chamber invited the parties to focus their submissions on the application for videolink testimony, since it considered this to be the next logical step. The Chamber explained its reasons for this on the 29th of October. On the 1st of November, 2007, counsel for Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Balaj requested the Chamber to reject the application for videolink testimony. Both submitted that it is not in the interests of justice that Mr. Kabashi testifies without being present in person before the Chamber and the accused. It's their position that the Chamber should be in a position to assess Mr. Kabashi's testimony without the impairments of videolink testimony. Mr. Brahimaj's counsel, Defence counsel, did not respond to the application.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have -- do apologise for interrupting, but it may only have been filed lately, but we have, indeed, responded and we have joined in the response of our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The response by Mr. Brahimaj's Defence counsel was not yet received by the Chamber. Mr. -- was it filed by 9.00 this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It was not filed by 9.00 this morning, Your Honour. So I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And it adds nothing to what has already been filed. I simply wish to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That we do join in their opposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances and the Chamber having considered the -- the opposition by other Defence counsel, will now continue -- will now continue with the decision, the reasons pronounced until now not being amended in any way. Under Rule 81 bis of the Tribunal's Rules, a Chamber may order that proceedings be conducted by way of videolink if that is consistent with the interests of justice. The Chamber considers that Mr. Kabashi is an important eye-witness to crimes charged in the indictment and that all measures capable of securing his testimony before the Tribunal in The Hague in the near future are exhausted. Although the Chamber agrees with the Haradinaj, the Balaj, and the Brahimaj Defence that it is preferable to hear a witness in court, the Chamber considers that testimony by videolink does not necessarily negatively impact the Chamber's ability to assess a witness's testimony. Should the Chamber conclude, after hearing Mr. Kabashi's testimony, that this is the case, this factor could affect the weight that the Chamber will attach to the evidence. The Chamber finds that under the given circumstances, videolink testimony is consistent with the interests of justice, and therefore grants the application. The accused will be allowed more than the usual amount of time in cross-examination of this witness. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's application for compelled videolink for Shefqet Kabashi. Then, Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness back in the courtroom. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just indicate over the adjournment we have identified another document from the file which was produced by this witness which is relevant, and Mr. Guy-Smith has very kindly offered to allow me with the Trial Chamber's permission to nibble into five minutes of what would have been his cross-examination time to deal with one additional document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless I was mistaken, it was not indicated as one of the documents to be used by the Defence in cross-examination. I didn't have time to check because I've just received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's absolutely correct, it was not notified in advance, it was not anticipated in advance of being used, it arises out of one of the Judge's questions and answers in connection to material that is to be found in the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, the Bench being blamed for --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The time -- did I say the Judge's questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I try to be a serious person, I now and then -- I just wanted to explain to Mr. Dutertre that it was apparently one of the Judge's questions that triggered the issue which unless you would disagree, Mr. Dutertre, might show --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in your hands, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I am clarifying it because when I said the Judge's questions, I'm afraid I was again slipping -- suffering from a slip of the tongue. It was the answer by the witness to one of my questions which prompted this search of the documentation. It's not a document the Prosecution are not aware of; it comes from their own exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what it is. And as with the five -- the six exhibits you tendered, Mr. Dutertre, the Chamber will of course first have to look what the consequences are of using this exhibit, and then decide whether it will admit it as it did with the five documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, once the witness has entered the courtroom --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you may continue to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the meantime perhaps the Trial Chamber could have hard copy documents, a copy for the witness as well possibly. Mr. Registrar, does the witness have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, I want to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, first of all, our apologies for a delayed start. We had to deal with a few urgent procedural matters. I hope you'll have understanding for this. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, I want to take this as briefly as I can. You need to look at the paper that has just been handed to you. You need to only concern yourself with the paper that appears in front of the yellow sticker, which is the original B/C/S version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, as far as numbers are concerned --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it already --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It hasn't. I think Mr. Registrar indicated that the appropriate way of dealing with it is for it to be allocated the next Defence MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, this is a document that you supplied to the Prosecution from the Pec district court, and I want you to just help us with it first of all so we understand what it is. If you look to the very end of the document you can see that it is stamped and signed under the name of Zoran Babic, deputy public prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it a request then from the deputy public prosecutor to the district court investigating judge to open an investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And we can see - and this is something I'd like you to just focus on for a moment - the request itself is dated the 9th of September, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's stamped by the district court as being received as well on the 9th of September, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that stamp, does it look to you to be authentic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can just look first of all at the request as it appears, it's a request to open an investigation into the men whose names we've been considering, and we can see -- can you confirm for us, please, that as regards the first -- the first three named individuals, Zenelj Alija, Bekim Kalamashi, and Smajl Smajli, this request notes that they are at large, whereas in respect of the other individuals numbered 4 to 11, each of them is recorded as being in custody. Can you confirm that, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that this is indeed what it says here. Whether the same information exists in the case file, I don't know, yes, but indeed it does say here "remains at large and in custody."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And if we can just look, please, at the end of the document above the prosecutor's signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see that he makes a number of recommendations under the headings "I recommend," and I'd like you to look, please, at the fourth paragraph, that's the second of the two large paragraphs there. It appears to be a recommendation that all of the reported men should be remanded in custody under Article 191 of the code, and then it goes on in the English translation: "Considering that Zenelj Alija and Bekim Kalamashi remain at large and since there is a fear that if the other reported men are released they would be beyond the reach of state organs and a fear that they would continue to perpetrate the crime of which they are suspected." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So again just to pull this together, this is a document from the public prosecutor which records that Zenelj Alija and Bekim Kalamashi are not in custody; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know at all whether Mr. Babic had any involvement in the canal investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He did? What was his involvement --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What was his involvement in the canal investigation, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present on the 10th of September as the deputy district public prosecutor. That's what the records indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you help us at all as to any reason that you might know of why deputy public prosecutor would record those two men as being not in custody if in fact they were in custody?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness is asked to speculate; therefore, objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. If that is the objection, the way the question is put is whether or not there is any explanation of which the judge is aware of why in this case -- if I can put it in that rather more concrete way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you first ask the witness if he is aware of any reason, and then if he is aware of what the reason would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, are you aware of any particular reason why in this case the public prosecutor who was at the canal would record in a document dated and received by your court on the 9th that two men were not in custody if in fact they were in custody of the police and had been responsible for pointing out the canal to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I cannot categorically state why the deputy public prosecutor wrote this. I can guess that he wrote what he did on the basis of the documents he had before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
