utterances.text: Can I ask you this: As the deputy public prosecutor present at the canal, would he have been allowed to talk to the police officers about how they discovered it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did -- or actually, it's not that I think. I'm sure he didn't talk to them about this. Besides, I believe you should speak to him and ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, the question was whether he would be allowed to talk with the police officers about this, not whether he did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The organs of the MUP and the prosecutor's offices cooperate one with another, they have close cooperation about the detection, uncovery, and prosecution of perpetrators of crimes. That's why I wanted to read out to you the legal provisions governing the different duties these bodies have.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And finally on that last point, Mr. Gojkovic, before the prosecutor decides to request the opening of an investigation, would you expect him to familiarise himself with the content of any interrogations that had been conducted by the police?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before a filing or request for an investigation, the prosecutor receives a criminal report from the police together with the supporting documentation. These individuals were first suspects, now they were indictees. If there is any material evidence about that, it is also enclosed in that documentation. In addition to that, if any statements were taken from individuals as eye-witnesses or merely citizens, these statements would be attached to that documentation as well. Once the prosecutor receives all the material, he makes the decision as to whether to issue a request to open an investigation or to send the criminal report back to the police for further supplementing of the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the answer to my question, Mr. Gojkovic, is yes, is that correct, you would expect him to see the statements that had been made by the accused whilst in police custody, just yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prosecutor must examine all the enclosed evidence and make a decision based upon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I look, please, now with you at paragraphs 92 and 93 of your statement where you deal with the investigation and prosecution of two men called Krist and Lek Pervorfi. And again I'm going to take this as quickly as I can with you, Mr. Gojkovic. Paragraph 92 you indicate that you know about the investigation into those two men because the Pec district court was asked by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on the request of The Hague Tribunal to submit a report on their interview. This is paragraphs 92 and 93. My question is: Do you have any knowledge of this case independent of the papers before we move on? Do you have any recollection of this case?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any recollection of the case, no, absolutely not, unless there are rulings in which I took part as member of the bench that decided on the possible extensions of detention. And I mentioned that, I believe, in paragraph 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there. I'm sorry. Your answer is a little difficult to follow. Either you have a recollection of it or you don't. Do you now have any recollection of this case, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in what sense you mean of the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember it --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the case as such exists in the records --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "you have a recollection or not," it appears that the witness at this moment has no recollection, but he does not exclude for the possibility that if he would see documents that matters might come back in his mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how we understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's my understanding as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But we see at paragraph 93 that you indicate that you were present -- president of the court and presided over a panel of three judges who extended their detention by two months, following the original one-month investigative detention, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this. I stated that and I confirm it now. The register states the number of the case, the persons to whom the case was assigned. As of November 1998, I was the president of the court. If the detention was extended by two months, then I definitely was one of the judges on the bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was telling you that if there was such an extension, then a document to that effect must exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Just pause with me for a moment. We don't see on the annexes to your statement the decision of extension, but do I understand you to be saying if their detention was extended you must have been the person responsible because at that stage you were president. Is that how we understand the testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, because according to the rules of procedure the president of the court is ex officio president of the KV panel --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which is the panel deciding about the extension of detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You then go on to say after that the Supreme Court of Serbia extended their detention for three more months. Again, is that based on recollection or on consulting the records?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the papers. I wasn't able to. I explained to you what the procedure was. I have a letter here which states what they were asking from me and how I responded to that. If you want me to, I can read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, I'm not asking you to read out a letter from the Office of the Prosecutor, but your statement records the fact that it is --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the prosecutor, you misunderstand me. That's the letter from the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Foreign Affairs where they asked me to send as a matter of urgency certified statements from the investigation of Pervorfi Krist, and the other one, I don't know what his name is. It says there that I heard them, but I replied to this request of theirs on the basis of the court register which has the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm only asking you a very simple question. Where you say here in your statement: "After that the Supreme Court of Serbia extended their detention for three more months ..." From where do you get that information about the decision that was made in this case?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last sentence of paragraph 93, this can be checked in the records. This information is given on the basis of the court register.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so my question is simple: Did you check the register before writing the statement? Is that how you got the information?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I have been able to respond to that letter if not by consulting the register? I consulted the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That was all I was seeking to establish with you. Now, I want to ask you, please, if you would, to look at a document which has not yet been introduced into evidence, and I'm just going to give you the reference number for it. It is Defence document 1D69001, and it is a municipal court judgement concerning the case of Lek Pervorfi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it will need a number I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It will, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification as D192.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could -- first of all, Mr. Gojkovic, you can confirm, please, can you, that the document that you're looking at on the right-hand side of the screen is a decision of the municipal court in Sremska Mitrovica concerning the case of the accused Lek Pervorfi from Dujak?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because this case did not come from the Pec district court or from the courts within the jurisdiction of that district court.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, could you just help us to interpret it, please, because it is a document that the Prosecution have provided from communication with Belgrade. I just want you to look at the word "judgement," please, and confirm that this is a judgement dated the 13th of August, 1999, recording a conviction against Lek Pervorfi for the offence of possessing a fire-arm, that is a pistol, and ammunition. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the criminal offence of -- for the possession of unlicensed weapons --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and it was obviously committed within the jurisdiction of the Sremska Mitrovica district court, whereas in that other case within the Pec district court they were responsible for a different crime. In paragraph 92 of my statement you can find this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, please don't run ahead of yourself because the evidence that you're giving at the moment is inconsistent with the text of the judgement itself which makes it clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I understood the witness to say where in his statement he referred to a case against Krist and Lek Pervorfi, that this judgement might be in a different case. That is how I understood him, so therefore how on the basis of the crime described that is inconsistent is not clear to me yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I thought that the witness's answer was that this was in a different geographical jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's then perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because if you look at the judgement itself under the words "is guilty" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He then referred: "Whereas in that other case within the Pec district court they were responsible for a different crime" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore I have difficulties in understanding how this judgement --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I can develop it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What the witness has indicated at page 54, line 24, is that this offence was an unlicensed weapons offence obviously committed within the jurisdiction of the Sremska Mitrovica court. And in fact, if one looks at the judgement itself, it makes it clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please develop your -- let's not try to -- we've had some difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you look at the judgement itself where it makes it clear that Lek Pervorfi is found guilty because from an undetermined day in 1996 until the 28th of October, 1998, in his house in Dujak village, Djakovica, he held, without authorisation, a Walther 7.65-millimetre pistol with a serial number and ammunition. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On an undetermined day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On an undetermined day, Mr. Gojkovic, up to, if you look at it on the 28th of October, 1998 --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what the judgement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was the day that Mr. Pervorfi was arrested in the proceedings that brought him before your court for the extension of his detention I suggest. Could I ask you just for the sake of clarification -- as I say, it's better to read it before we're running ahead. If you could please look at the third paragraph from the end of the judgement which is the sentencing section which explains how the court has reached its decision on sentencing. So for that purpose we need to go to the -- in the B/C/S version it's page 3 and in the English version it is page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: But for sake of clarity, the court you said? Which court are you speaking of, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This court, the court that has delivered this judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Explains its sentencing decision by reference to the periods of time spent in custody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As authorised we would submit by Judge Gojkovic, Mr. Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just take it reasonably swiftly. Could you read, please, to yourself, Mr. Gojkovic, the paragraph that appears in the centre of the page there, so as you look at the screen, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we could expand that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just read that paragraph to yourself --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps just make it a bit -- that's as big as it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and read -- digest what it is indicating for us, please. Have you had a chance to look at that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My response --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I haven't asked you a question yet. I haven't yet asked you a question. Please bear with me for a moment. Have you read the paragraph, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it all --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I can repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just wait for the question, if you will, please. Taking it very shortly, I just want a summary of what that is indicating to us. It is indicating, is it not, that this court is refusing to take into account in sentencing Mr. Pervorfi for the fire-arms offence the period of time that he spent in custody of the Pec district court following his original arrest for the crime of terrorism under Article 125?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wonder what is the relevance of all these questions in relation to our case. I may be ahead of myself, but I don't know where Mr. Emmerson wants to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where he's heading for, but he seems to take some distance from our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It goes to the withdrawal of the terrorism charges against Lek Pervorfi and Krist Pervorfi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's further hear the evidence. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Judge Gojkovic -- I'm sorry, Mr. Gojkovic, let's put a different question to you and see if it's easier to approach in this way. Do you see halfway down this paragraph a sentence that indicates that the investigation against Lek Pervorfi for the crime of terrorism was suspended by decision KI67/99 of the 29th of July, 1999, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I follow it up with three sentences to clear it all up?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The case was with the district court of Pec. By decisions of the competent authorities of the Ministry of Justice and the Supreme Court of Serbia, it was decided that the district court of Sremska Mitrovica should hear the case. What were the reasons, I don't know. I suppose that they had been detained there after we had moved out of Kosovo. What was going on there during the proceedings I cannot say. I suppose that the prosecutor changed the qualification of crimes committed, and I'm stating that based on the description of the crime. As to the rest of the proceedings, well for that one would have to review the entire case file of the district court of Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We don't necessarily need to go quite that far, Mr. Gojkovic. The decision of suspension on the 29th of July, 1999, was a decision to terminate charges of terrorism, was it not? That's what it indicates?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it reads, then there must be a decision in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No discussion there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. So could we please look then at that decision which is Defence 1D690059.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the translation on this document is unofficial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And still needs a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And still needs a number, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, would you consider that document, please, Mr. Gojkovic, because it's the same reference number as we see in the judgement, KI67/99, and it's dated, as you see, the 29th of July.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that is a decision which describes -- is described as a decision to suspend the investigation against Krist and Lek Pervorfi, and it's a decision made under Article 170 of the Yugoslav code on criminal procedure, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Article 170 provides that the examining magistrate is required to dismiss an inquiry if the prosecutor decides not to pursue a prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, that's what the law prescribes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And so the decision that we're looking at here is a decision to abandon against Lek and Krist Pervorfi charges of terrorism, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the decision was to terminate the proceedings since the public prosecutor decided not to pursue the case any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the one from Sremska Mitrovica --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, this is not the one from Sremska Mitrovica, is it, this is the decision of your case that is suspended. If you look at the decision, it's the investigating judge from the direct court in Sremska Mitrovica, but the decision suspends, that is, terminates, the investigation which was initiated following the decision of the Pec district court, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation is terminated by a decision of the district court of Sremska Mitrovica as part of the case heard by the Pec court that was forwarded to the Sremska Mitrovica case because the prosecutor decided not to press the matters any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's just draw the threads together. These men were held in custody of the Pec district court on charges of terrorism, and you've told us that you extended their detention for a period of time. Then in July of 1999 the prosecution against them for terrorism was terminated, and then as we can see in the judgement that we just looked at, Lek Pervorfi was prosecuted for possession of a fire-arm up to and including the time of his arrest on the 29th of October, 1998, but the court was not willing to take into account in the sentence for that offence the period of time he'd spent in custody to the Pec district court on the terrorism charges that the prosecution had abandoned; correct? That's a summary of the position, is it not? Do you want me to go through it again? Would it -- did my question not come through clearly? Mr. Gojkovic, what I'm doing, inviting you to confirm, is a summary of what these two documents indicate to us. And what they indicate is that a prosecution or investigation, rather, of these two men for the crime of terrorism under section -- Article 125 of the Criminal Code was abandoned on the 29th of July, after they had been held in the custody of the Pec district court under the detention authorisations that you've told us about, and then prosecution was pursued against Lek Pervorfi for possession of a fire-arm which was seized from him at the time of his arrest on the 28th of October, 1998, but the sentencing court was not prepared to count the time spent in custody on the terrorism charges, which were abandoned, as part of the sentence for the possession of a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered these questions of yours, but I'll answer it again. This document pertaining to the suspension of any further investigation is a document of the district court of Sremska Mitrovica, as part of the case of the Pec district, that was forwarded to the Sremska Mitrovica court, and this came about because the prosecutor abandoned the charges. As to how it came about that they were finally being prosecuted for illegal possession of weapons, I don't know, but here we have an official document before us and this is the extent of the things I can confirm to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith. By the way, if you would allow, we're now in the middle of these documents so I would like to ask one additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson has put to you what these documents tell us, dropping terrorist charges, convicted for possession of fire-arms, pre-trial detention in the terrorist case not deduced in the fire-arms case. Now, may I ask you, would you consider it a possibility that the fire-arms charges were more or less deduced from or were a reduction from terrorist charges? Did that happen? Did you charge someone with terrorism and that you might find yourself in evidentiary problems and that you would down-size the case and make it an illegal possession of arms case? Is that something that happened in your jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I categorically state that this case here is a unique one. It -- a thing like that never happened with the district court of Pec, whether an accused is guilty or not needs to be determined, but I can only suppose that the court in agreement with the prosecutor decided to opt for a different qualification of crimes committed, upon prosecution's request. I am stating this based on the fact that the crime was committed in October 1998 in a village in the environs of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you, this judgement is about the possession of fire-arms from 1996 to the end of October 1998, isn't it, not just 1998? Or did I misinterpret the judgement? It could be put on your screen again if you would like to see it again. Mr. Registrar, I think it was D192 if I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, whilst it's brought up, it may be self-evident, but from the passage in the judgement concerning sentence it is plain that Mr. Pervorfi had been in custody continuously between his arrest on the 29th of October and the judgement of the sentencing court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm contesting that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I thought the witness said it was a judgement on the crime committed in October 1998, whereas he is found guilty because from an undetermined day in 1996 until - so that covers a far larger period than just October 1998, that's at least how I understand this judgement, and therefore I just sought clarification of the testimony where you said it was a crime committed in 1998. Perhaps -- may I ask the question in the following way: Let's just assume that on the basis of possession of fire-arms in circumstances which would allow for the suspicion that there was activity undermining the state authority, which I understand was called terrorism at the time, if finally later on in the proceedings it would be difficult to prove that this was -- this intent was -- could be associated with the possession, the illegal possession of arms, what would you do under those circumstances? Would you drop the terrorist charges and charge for illegal possession of arms or would you change the qualification of the facts charged and not drop the charges, but just change the qualification? Do you understand what I'm trying to find out, how I have to interpret this judgement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This judgement should be viewed as an easier path that was before the court. Currently I don't have before me the law regulating the issue of statute of limitations. If the offence began being committed in 1996, I wonder whether there is any statute of limitation applicable and whether these people can be prosecuted at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's an interesting observation. Therefore, I take it that terrorist activity would under the statute of limitation, would -- you would be allowed to prosecute that for a longer period of time. But at least this Court apparently has considered that there was or at least assumed that there was no statute of limitation applicable. Now, is -- my question is: Is it under your law applicable at that time, was it possible just to drop charges and, as you said, take an easier path, perhaps something that would be easier to prove? Because if fire-arms are seized during a search, it might be easier to prove illegal possession of fire-arms than it would be to prove terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the cases I worked on this did not occur. Either there was an offence or there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Any questions, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, my headphones are broken so it takes a minute to -- that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to start, Mr. Gojkovic, just with really a housekeeping matter to tidy something up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have D66 which is a video played for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at this video, sir. In this video there is a gentleman in it wearing a suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And like, if you could for purposes of the record, identify that individual I believe as you well know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You could stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you identify that individual, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is me, Gojkovic, Radomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Guy-Smith, could you tell us what was shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was a video that was previously shown with regard to a visit at Gllogjan on September 16th in which Mr. Kaufmann and Mr. Achilleas Pappas were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, if it ever comes to the Appeals Chamber, where do we find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's D66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's D66, I might have missed that, and at least what we see on the screen that it bears -- the image bears the date of 16th of ninth, 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I believe it's about the counter of 1.18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the time indicated on the screen is 14.50. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go back for a moment just to make sure that there's some understandings about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I would like if we could have P1200 up on the screen, and I believe it will be page 17 in the English translation and page 16 in the B/C/S. And directing your attention when it comes up to -- no. It's going to be page -- it starts on -- actually on page 15 in B/C/S and then it goes over to page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like you to take a look at the bottom of page 15, the very last line, and then moving over to page 16 in B/C/S. That is the part of the judgement that relates to the finding of nitrate traces on the hands of a number of the accused, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the judge in question wrote down; that is what he based his decision on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could now have up on the screen P1201, and I apologise because I'm not sure precisely what page it's going to come up. It's, as I have it, pages, I believe -- I believe it's going to be pages 13 and 14, which is findings of the expert. And really all I'm looking for is the very last page which has a signature on it, a gentleman whose name is Slavisa Jankovic. Okay. And for the B/C/S ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature as being the chemist Slavisa Jankovic, who was the individual who did a fair amount of testing with regard to nitrate traces during 1998 and specifically for the Pec court? He also did work I believe in 1999.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states that this person signed the document, that he did it as a forensic expert. Those are probably the facts of the case, however I cannot tell you anything about it since I didn't work on the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate that. My question is: Do you recognise the signature? Is this a gentleman that you worked with, Slavisa Jankovic. Is he one of the experts working at your courthouse during this time?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since she was designated as forensic expert, she must have been on the list. The court could not have engaged her in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, the question was whether you recognised the signature, but Mr. Guy-Smith may have confused you by adding a lot of things. But do you recognise -- have you seen that signature before, do you recognise it as the signature of that expert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you that. I don't remember ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember Slavisa Jankovic offering expert testimony in the Pec courts during 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. She wasn't in any of my cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was there a case tried in the Pec district court concerning the Djakovica Group in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several cases. I don't know which one you're referring to specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, this is a case in which there was proof that 143 accused individuals, according to the judgement, had participated in the event because of positive results from paraffin testing. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know as a president of the court that the case existed. Others were seized of it, and what exactly was going on in that case I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have up on the screen -- and this is going to need an MFI number, 2D001534.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be D194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm referring to what would be page 38 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm going to read something to you and see whether or not you're aware of this comment being made, and this is under the section called "hearing of evidence" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Which page, please, in the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Page 30 -- that would be page 38 in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Also page 38?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have it as page 38 in the English translation here. It's -- there we go. Perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I just want to draw your attention to one part which will be the second full paragraph for the moment: "The chemist Slavisa Jankovic, employee of the Pristina MUP who has conducted analysis in most Albanian cases during the trial of the so-called 'Djakovica Group' said: 'It is not possible to determine what was the origin of the nitrate while regarding the nitrates with determined origin: Whether from powder particles or urine or spray or cosmetic products or some other material ... There aren't any possibilities to make a distinction of the solution in regard to some characteristics, shade, link. They are the same.'" Now, my question to you, sir, is: During these hearings and you as the president of the Pec tribunal, did you have a policy where your judges engaged in questioning or further understanding as to how such physical evidence was obtained and the reliability of it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judges proceed in the case, whether in the role of investigating judges or presidents of benches. When at any stage of the proceedings they order that an expert witness file a report, they have to order that particular expert witness what precisely he or she is supposed to report on. These specific instructions are sent to the expert witness who on the basis of it all, of the evidence that is also sent to him, provides his expertise. If his findings are incomplete or unclear, the expert witness may be called to appear in order to clarify all the important facts or, in the alternative --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, sir, with regard to the expert opinion of Slavisa Jankovic in the document we looked at just a moment ago, P1201, the opinion is there are traces of nitrates and nitrites which can come from gunpowder. That was the opinion rendered, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that this was her opinion. What happened later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. That was the opinion rendered by the expert, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that it is possible that this is her opinion. What happened later, whether this opinion was confirmed, varied, or whether another expert report was sought, this is something you will be able to find in the case file.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. If that was the case, then what we would find with regard to the judgement rendered is some reference, as we find in the judgement that we have, to another expert report, wouldn't we? There would be some indication that there had been another expert report, correct, and we don't have that here, do we? And by that I'm referring to the judgement. We may need to move back to P1200. Unless you want to take my word for it that the only mention of an expert report with regard to the issue of any kind of nitrate traces is expert witness number 234-1-554/98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, could you please come to your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did -- do you, to your knowledge, know whether in this particular judgement there was information given to the judge as to when the test was taken, as to who took the test --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question because the witness is asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, he is not asked to speculate. He's asked whether he knows whether information was given to the judge. Do you remember or do you not remember, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my answer. A judgement is rendered not on the basis of a single piece of evidence but on the basis of all the available evidence. Furthermore, I cannot comment on this particular expert report in that case because I was not seized of the case. I knew of the case, but I would have to be able to look at the entire case file to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, it is -- it goes without saying that when rendering a judgement that you should consider all the evidence, so that's understood by -- especially by all lawyers in this courtroom. You're not asked to comment on it. The simple was: Do you know whether any specific -- let me -- whether in this particular case - I take it, Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that there was information given to the judge as to when the test was taken, who took the test, do you know that, if such information was given to the judge, yes or no; if you don't know, tell us. If you do know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours I'd like if --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption. We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm trying to get done with the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last question, Mr. Guy-Smith. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like if you could explain to the Chamber what you meant when you said in your statement in 2006: "The Albanians settle their quarrels by death. It is their rule of nature." Could you explain to the Chamber, please, what do you mean by the Albanians' rule of nature?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said this, I meant that there were certain blood-feuds at the time of the tragic events that happened in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey -- of course I'm looking at the clock and it would be time for a break. At the same time, I do not know what the result will be for any protective measures for the next witness. And since -- if they would be granted they would have to be prepared over a break. So therefore, although it by and large would be the time to have a break, I don't know how much time you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I don't want to heighten the tension or the expectation any longer. I have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, any further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One very brief question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gojkovic, in July -- in July 1999, when the charges for terrorism were dropped, the charges against the -- against the Pervorfi, Serbian authorities were no longer in Kosovo, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And you no longer could access the witnesses and you were no longer able to collect evidence on the scene?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the two questions I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Mr. Gojkovic, since the Chamber has no further questions for you, this concludes your testimony. At the same time, you're looking at me as if you would like to say something. Is that -- if not, I'd like to thank you -- is there any matter because Mr. Emmerson in the beginning said if you want to draw our attention to certain articles of criminal procedure -- although we are more interested in what actually happened rather than the exact framework of the law because we will not decide whether and who stayed within the -- within the boundaries of the law. But if you would like to add something, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only wish to make a few points. First, I'd like the Pervorfi case to be obtained in order for one to see what it contains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, if the parties would like to have that available, then they'll certainly ask for that and then the Chamber will consider whether or not to support that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second, one or two, keep in kind the decree on the application of the Law on Criminal Procedure in times of war, during a state of war. I can leave a copy for your benefit if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you leave a copy so that the parties can consult it -- and of course the law is, as such, accessible by a court even if not provided by the parties. We'll certainly consider your suggestion. If you leave a copy, that would certainly assist the parties in their decision whether or not to seek further attention of the Chamber to this piece of legislation. Any other point, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to answer all questions put to you by the parties and by the Court, and I wish you a safe trip home again, Mr. Gojkovic. The --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you and thank you for your hospitality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then in view of an application for protective measures, not in any way anticipating on the decision to be made by the Chamber, the Chamber would very much like to have everything prepared for such protective measures in case the Chamber might grant the application. We'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An application was filed for the next witness to have protective measures granted. I'd first like to go into private session to ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I remind the parties and myself to switch off our microphones whenever the witness answers questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While the witness is coming in there are three exhibits I think I'll be using with her. She will have a copy in hard copy before her especially the Human Rights Watch report. There weren't -- there was no need to copy large volumes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. -- We are in open session at this moment. A redaction will be made. Witness 28, because that's how we will call you, Witness 28, the Chamber has decided to grant the application for protective measures, that is, that you'll testify under pseudonym, we'll call you Witness 28; that your image will be distorted so that outside of this courtroom people will not recognise your face; and that your voice will be distorted as well so that they would not recognise your voice. But your testimony as such is public. If there would ever come any point where by answering questions you would fear that you would reveal your identity, then you can ask for private session. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 28. Please be seated. The curtains will be drawn up, again that you're shielded by. Witness 28, you'll first be examined by Mr. Re, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have a witness pseudonym sheet which is MFI 65 ter 2138. As we are in private session, is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are not? Glad I asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness 28, I want you to have a look at a document which is on the screen in front of you, or should be, it's 65 ter 2138. I just want you to confirm that it has your name, date of birth, place of birth, and those details are correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number to be assigned to it. The pseudonym sheet under seal would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P1210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness 28, in front of you, you have a hard copy of a statement dated the 28th of October, 2007, which has a 65 ter number which I will tell you in a moment. I just want you to have a look at the statement, it's not being publicly shown, it has your number in front of it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, if you give already the 65 ter number then Mr. Registrar could prepare for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It is 2132, under seal, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and we will file a publicly redacted one now that we've agreed with the Defence on redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be -- of course the public version will be available to the public. Yes. Yes -- no, I see it's on the -- on the transcript it appears as if the witness assigns the number to the document. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness 28, I just want you to have a look at the statement. Does it bear your signature and is it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And would you give the same evidence of everything that's contained in those 100 -- I'm sorry, 97 paragraphs with two taken out in this court if you were asked to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On that basis may it be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I made a mistake earlier when a number was assigned, it was a number to the pseudonym sheet and not to the 92 ter statement. Mr. Registrar, the 92 ter statement would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P1211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I do understand that there are no objections, in view of the agreed redactions and one correction, therefore P1211 is admitted into evidence, under seal, public version to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What follows is the summary of the Rule 92 ter statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you explained to Witness 28 what the meaning of the summary is?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh. We read the summary of your statement so that the public knows about what the testimony approximately is and not just a piece of paper, where most people would not go and try to find that piece of paper. So just a summary of what is in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And where is the summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It will be displayed in Sanction on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And the Prosecutor will read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1998 the witness worked as a human rights worker for (redacted), a Belgrade-based NGO --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Emmerson is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For technical reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: She travelled frequently to Kosovo to investigate crimes committed by both Albanians and Serbs. A Serb researcher investigated crimes committed against Serbs, and Albanian researchers interviewed crimes committed against Albanians. They travelled to areas of conflict to investigate whether crimes had been committed. In 1998 the witness was in Kosovo for about a week to ten days every month and, with the other researchers, investigated crimes committed in the Dukagjini area. In early March 1998 she attended the funeral of members of the Ahmeti family in Cirez/Likosane following a MUP attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, that's -- that's actually factual mistake. It was not in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness 28, I want to ask you some questions in relation to your statement of the 28th of February, 1998, and I want you to expand and clarify some of the matters there. Could you please turn to paragraphs 17, 18, and 19 concerning the attack in Cirez and Likosane on the 28th of February, 1998, and in particular paragraph 18 where you refer to several people, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In the sentence you say in the middle: "The funeral had an intense political background to it." What was it about the funeral which gave it that intense political background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: The number of the people present, the effort they all put to come together, thousands of people came, Albanian flags, the hills and the fields were all covered, the people -- although there was a fear that the Serbian police would major disrupt the way how they would achieve, soldiers in KLA uniforms present. I seen them mingling in the groups. I was far from the place where the speeches were given, but I had feeling that I was present to the real rise of rebellion and the new moment in Kosovo, historical moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, just pause there. In relation to the soldiers in KLA uniforms present, what -- just tell the Court what they added in your -- what you observed and how they added to the political background to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: I have the impression that they wanted really to show --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I hate to interrupt the witness, but I seem to be having some technical difficulties here. I'm not hearing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps since the witness is using the voice distortion microphone you might turn -- have to turn up the left volume button manner the usual one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The red one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I do apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I know we're a very long way from the start of this trial - I'm getting some feedback here - and the ruling the Trial Chamber has given in respect of another witness from this organization, but I do request Mr. Re to avoid matters of opinion, matters of speculation, and to lay the foundation for the testimony he can elicit. I'm not clear at all as to where this line of questioning goes. If it's goes to an issue of fact in the case or -- foundation for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time the witness answered in a rather factual way, as a matter of fact. Although it was--

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's the next question I was particularly concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Re ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you're invited to refrain from seeking opinion evidence. I take it that you understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Any opinion evidence the witness would give in our submission would of course after having laid the appropriate factual backgrounds would assist the Trial Chamber in its determination of the issues of conflict at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I will be very careful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you about, Witness, is the -- the presence of the KLA soldiers there, how in your view based upon what you saw it contributed to the political -- the political feeling at that funeral.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: As I said, I had feeling that it is uprising, that those few soldiers I have seen been proud, finally walking free through the mass of the people, they were actual supported by all of these people in -- who were present there. Is that what you asked me for, that's what my --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you about how the people there reacted to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: They'd been proud.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well -- and did -- I won't said "did." The report or what you observed there has made it into two separate reports, one was the "Spotlight" report, which is Exhibit 6 in this trial, Exhibit P5, I'm sorry, which is "Spotlight" report 26 at pages 3 and 4; and also the Human Rights Watch report, which is MFI -- sorry, not MFI, 65 ter 999 at pages -- at page 91, which is K0364881. Before I go further I'm just going to ask you, the information which you gathered by attending that event and talking to the people, as you described in paragraph 19, was that information used for both the "Spotlight" report and the Human Rights Watch report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: At that moment I was only employed by (redacted), so I can tell you that my interviews in Nebiu family have been used in (redacted) report. I can't recall this part really went in Human Rights Watch report, that I joined later, except if I can see it now and get reminded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please switch all microphones off while the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Likewise, if I could take you to the next paragraph which is paragraph 20 when you refer to the police operation being mounted against the Jashari family compound in Prekaz, and researchers from the (redacted) going shortly thereafter to investigate what had happened. Paragraph 21 you say: "I used the interviews to prepare the relevant portion of "Spotlight" report number 26."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could just - which is in the bundle with you - have a look at "Spotlight" report number 26, and that's Exhibit P6 in these proceedings at pages 5 to 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, is that the information -- was the information in that report based upon reports which you sent back from the field, to (redacted), in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: Our researchers, partly me and I prepared the text which then was worked on of course by director of organization.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could turn to paragraph 25 on the same page of your statement where you say: "Sources within the Serbian police told you that Adem Jashari was known within police circles as the Albanian Arkan."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that being displayed in Sanction for the Court? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just explain to the Trial Chamber, if you can, what is meant by or why they described him as the Albanian Arkan? What did they tell you which enabled you to write this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: As a background for this information, after massacre and crime committed by Serbian forces against Jashari family, I tried to investigate who actually did commit the crime, and during that investigation I had three different sources, police sources, explaining background and relationship between Adem Jashari and former chief of Srbica police station, if it is important at all for this case. And these sources were highly critical toward corrupted Serbian police chiefs in Mitrovica and Srbica and was telling me that basically they had been protecting for years Adem Jashari, who was Serbian -- like Albanian Arkan. I don't know do you remember who is Arkan. Arkan was paramilitary person in Serbia during 1990s, criminal background, went into different police operations, military operation in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is: Why were they referring to him as an Arkan? All the rest is in your statement. I just want you to concentrate on the Arkan bit. Why, of all people, Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/28
utterances.text: I suppose - but that's really opinion now - I suppose because there were issues with Adem Jashari getting very frequently into conflict with some neighbours, according to those sources, and being kind of tough guy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note the time. It appears to be just past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 28, we had a rather chaotic start. I apologise for that. We hope to be more quiet and more organized Monday when we continue. I hope that you're available on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do I have a choice?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there would be problems which will be insurmountable, the Chamber will -- certainly would listen to it and to see whether we can find a solution, but we are under quite some time pressure, because as you know your testimony had been scheduled for an earlier stage of the proceedings. And since we're now close to the end of the proceedings we have not a lot of manoeuvring room anymore. But could you come on Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I would like to proceed, to finish with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'd like to see you back on Monday, the 5th of November, at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in this same courtroom. And I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or whether still to be given, but we would like to see you back on Monday. We adjourn until Monday, the 5th of November, quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
